topic: Sequence of Groundwater Contamination by Over-Fertilization
questionText:
Arrange the environmental steps leading to groundwater nitrate contamination from intensive agricultural fields:
(I) Excess synthetic urea fertilizer is broadcast onto agricultural fields beyond crop assimilation capacity
(II) Soil nitrifying bacteria convert excess ammonium (NH4+) into highly soluble, negatively charged nitrate ions (NO3-)
(III) Overhead flood irrigation dissolves the unabsorbed nitrate ions and carries them down through the soil profile
(IV) Nitrates percolate past the crop root zone into shallow water tables, elevating drinking-water nitrate levels above 45 mg/L

Choose the correct chronological/logical sequence from the options given below:

options.text: II -> I -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: I -> III -> II -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.text: IV -> II -> III -> I
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Nitrate pollution sequence: over-application of urea, microbial nitrification, leaching with irrigation water, and deep aquifer contamination.
Hence Option B is correct.
Hence, option (C) is correct.

questionText:
Match the AQI score range in List I with its official category in List II:

List I:
(A) 0 to 50
(B) 101 to 200
(C) 201 to 300
(D) 401 to 500

List II:
(I) Good (Minimal health impact)
(II) Moderate (Breathing discomfort to people with asthma and heart diseases)
(III) Poor (Breathing discomfort to most people on prolonged exposure)
(IV) Severe (Affects healthy people and seriously impacts those with existing diseases)
